_doc: THE WORKER ENVELOPE (V2-831 T-27). Background work shares the host with the voice, and a host that runs out of
memory freezes the voice first: on a small host with no swap, free memory can fall to zero while errands run,
the VAD falls behind real time and the host freezes. Every number here is a RATIO of what the host measures at
run time (psutil), never an absolute for one machine, so the same file holds on a laptop, a small server or a
large one. A deployment that needs other values writes `config/resources.json` beside this file (same keys).
A new worker waits for room with NO clock (V2-867): until the floor holds, the voice's shed ends and the worker
admitted before it RUNS — one at a time on a tight host; the operator's cancel is the exit, never a deadline.
The floor is the LARGER of `admit_free_ratio` of the total and `voice_reserve_mb`: the engine's measured RSS is
284-600 MB with the voice session embedded, so 768 MB keeps its peak plus a margin free for the voice; on a 4 GB
host the ratio (~780 MB) and the reserve agree, on a 2 GB host the ratio alone (~410 MB) would not hold one voice.
`voice_lag_s` is the voice's own lag bound (T-30): over it, an event, one spoken notice and load shed.
`loop_lag_s` is the BODY loop's bound (E0): a beat that wakes later than this is a host stall — recorded, one
`health` event, a quiet shed and ladder pressure; a turn waiting through it blames neither model nor provider.
THE SELF WATCHDOG (T-28): a thread beats the server loop; `freeze_s` without an answer, or free memory under
`pause_free_ratio`, sheds load; still so after `stuck_s` and under a supervisor (ZAELAR_SUPERVISED=1) it exits
non-zero for a restart, ended hard `exit_grace_s` later if the loop cannot shut down. A loop that answers while the
HOST is short of memory is the machine's notice, said at most once per `machine_notice_s` (V2-887).
`summary_push_s` (T-31): how often the compact summary goes to ZAELAR_SUMMARY_URL, when a deployment sets one.
`browser_bg_wait_s` (pass 10): how long a background search waits for HIS turn's search in the one browser.
THE VOICE RECYCLE (V2-871): the old LiveKit worker's close is waited `recycle_close_s`, then abandoned; the new one
must register within `recycle_verify_s`, retried `recycle_attempts` times `recycle_backoff_s` apart (doubling).
Gave up, or no live worker `voice_dead_s` after a session was asked for: an alert, and under a supervisor an exit
for a restart; unsupervised a new try every `recycle_retry_s`. `boot_grace_s` is the cold start (models, browser,
the first connection; a first session measured 2.5 min to listening on a small host): degraded marks and the
audio lag inside it are the warm-up, never a degradation.
A STARVED CPU (V2-872): between two heartbeats the host's steal share (/proc/stat) over `steal_pct_starved` %, or
any cgroup throttling (cpu.stat), makes that window's LiveKit marks the host's, not the worker's: an event, one
notice per episode, and never a recycle. Nor within `session_grace_s` of the last voice session's start.
PRESENCE AND SLEEP (V2-872): presence is a connected person: his input on a screen (a touch, a key, a typed line,
a spoken turn) or a VISIBLE tab with its stream open (its beat), never a stream open alone. A tab with no input
for `tab_sleep_min` closes its stream and waits for a gesture (0 = the tab never sleeps); the client reads the
value from the stream's hello. With an idle stop on (ZAELAR_IDLE_STOP_MIN), an engine nobody has come to since
boot or resume stops after `wake_grace_min` (ZAELAR_WAKE_GRACE_MIN overrides it) instead of the full window.
A CHEAP BOOT (V2-872): `prewarm_browser` warms the search Chromium at boot. A host that stops when idle wants it
false in its own `config/resources.json` (it pays the warm-up on every boot); undeclared there, it is already
false when ZAELAR_IDLE_STOP_MIN is set. The browser then starts at first use. `background_idle_every_s`: with no
screen open a passive widget's background tick runs at most this often, whatever its declared `every`.
LISTENING WHILE ASLEEP (V2-872 F2): an engine that reports when to be woken (`nucleo/pulse/wake.py`) asks for a
pass every `listen_every_min` only while something reacts to an inbound channel that can be caught up (a rule, a
waiting task, an errand, his notify preference — `nucleo/pulse/listeners.py`); with nothing listening, no pass.
THE VOICE IN ITS OWN PROCESS (V2-891). The voice (`python -m voice.engine`: LiveKit, the VAD, the ear, the mouth),
the body (`python -m server`), a Brain Worker and the browser each have a memory `budgets.<deployment>.<piece>`:
`mb` (what it should hold) and `ceiling_mb` (past it the voice process is recycled BETWEEN sessions). The deployment
is `cloud` when the engine serves a hosted account (ZAELAR_USER_ID) and `local` otherwise (ZAELAR_DEPLOYMENT names
it). `free_floor` is the free memory the host keeps before a new worker starts, and replaces
`admit_free_ratio`/`voice_reserve_mb` as the worker floor wherever this block is declared: what its `pieces` need
(their `ceiling_mb` summed, plus `mb` as the reserve), never more than `ratio`×total and never under `mb`. The ratio
is a CAP, not the floor: 20 % of a 48 GB laptop (9.6 GB) held every errand with ordinary apps open, while the
pieces need ~3.4 GB; on a 2-8 GB host the cap is what binds, so the older rule and the voice reserve hold there.
`pressure_pieces` (+ `mb`), capped by `pause_free_ratio`×total, is where the host is SHORT: the newest worker
pauses and the watchdog sheds. Without `pieces`/`pressure_pieces` the older ratios hold.
`priorities.<role>`: nice and OOM score per process (the voice served first and killed last, the browser killed
first); raising either needs no privilege, lowering one does, so an unprivileged host keeps what it could set.
`shed_ladder`: the rungs the engine gives memory back with, in order, one per heartbeat under pressure (free memory
under the floor), released in reverse once free memory is back over floor × `shed_recover_ratio`.
`embed_budget_ms`: how long a recall waits for a LOCAL embedding (a model on this machine, which pages in from
swap on a host short of memory) before it reads the lexical channel alone; a remote embedder keeps the turn's own
recall budget (ZAELAR_RECALL_BUDGET_MS).
